body.rationale: IPS status: ratified per the brief, so the hard breaches count. This is not the draft or owner_approved with faculty sign-off outstanding wording from the instructions, so I treat the limits as binding. I am black_litterman and excluded myself. I ranked on IPS compliance first, then on covariance-based methods, which §4.3 says fit a late-cycle regime better than return-forecast methods. Reviewer technical errors were the third criterion. 1) resampled_efficient_frontier: it has no hard breaches and has the broadest spread of the compliant return-driven books (effective N 13.1, Sharpe 0.42). Resampling damps the CMA estimation error that the reviews of my own and max_sharpe's equilibrium inputs flagged. Its weak point is the thin drawdown margin (-24.84% against -25%), which both reviewers noted, so I rank it first but not unconditionally. 2) cvar_minimization: it is compliant, with the best backtest Sharpe (0.74) and a shallow drawdown (-18.7%). Its intra-category reviewer called it a clean execution. The cost is concentration (about 2.9 effective assets) and volatility tuned exactly to the 8.00% floor, so it is a sleeve to blend, not a lone portfolio. 3) inverse_volatility: it is compliant, diversified (N 14.8) and needs no return forecast. Reviewers noted that it ignores correlation across about 43% credit and sovereign exposure. 4) tail_risk_parity: it is a covariance-based downside method from the non_traditional family, which helps the three-family span. It breaches only volatility (7.67% against an 8% floor) and its arithmetic reconciled. 5) risk_parity: it is similar and breaches only volatility slightly (7.56%). The reviews say it gives no risk-contribution output and that its effective N measures capital dispersion, not risk dispersion. First beats fifth because resampled_efficient_frontier passes every hard IPS limit and has the higher expected return. risk_parity breaches the volatility floor and its diversification claim cannot be verified from the proposal. I flag market_cap_weight. Its -40.6% backtest drawdown is 15.6 points beyond the limit, and the CRO risk score is 0.80, the worst in the field. Its weights are ETF AUM, not a market portfolio, and they double-count overlapping US style funds. It is about 77% equity, which is the wrong posture for a late-cycle regime. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier. It is orthogonal by design and its own proposal calls it a diagnostic.
